justification: Arguing each: A fails because no price for drying is ever given (only “at so much per ton per point of moisture” in passing); B names one thread only — Grendisham’s “On an unmanned site at two in the morning, that is when somebody looked out of a window” — not the whole; C is absent. The text opens on a settled rule, “the tall machine with the ducts inside is the one that burns” and “The explanation is as settled as the count,” then gives most of its length to Calverend, Grendisham and Steadgrove disagreeing about why. D captures both halves exactly.

The swab result is stated once: “per square foot the mixed-flow dryers carried what the cross-flow columns carried, within a few percent.” That kills A (reverses it) and C (nothing is said about new ducts being clean; the sample was “twenty-six machines that had never burned”). D fails because nobody in the passage attacks the sample — Steadgrove “accepts the swabs” and the writer says “The swabs are hard to walk past.” B is the plain reading.

Grendisham’s point is about what the second timestamp records: “The other time in the file is the moment the call came in... that is when somebody looked out of a window, not when anything caught,” and “It looks late because nobody was there to see it early.” A is the opposite of her claim that the two numbers only look aligned when “Set those two numbers side by side”; B and D are never said — she disputes the reading of the times, not their coverage or purpose. C.

Steadgrove’s date-sort is the source: “Sort the same sixty-one fires by date rather than by machine, and the machine stops mattering,” with “Forty-nine fall in a nine-day stretch at the tail of each harvest, when the deduction schedule bites hardest and the elevator’s delivery window is closing.” B is contradicted by the arithmetic (forty-nine of sixty-one, not every fire); C overreaches beyond anything claimed, and the writer notes Steadgrove’s remedy “is not the mutual’s to give”; D (grain arriving faster than dryers can take it) is never stated. A is what “the machine stops mattering” implies — the same commercial squeeze regardless of equipment.

The writer states her position outright in the last paragraph: “Until then Calverend’s account fits the evidence without having been tested by it,” preceded by “Grendisham’s objection has not been answered, and it cannot be answered from files like these.” A is excluded by that same sentence, B by the fact that she does adjudicate (“The swabs are hard to walk past”), and D by “nobody has worked out how to check” before next harvest. C.

Gap (1) completes a fixed collocation, “to take the long ___,” after “which puts the bottom of the list twelve years from a key” — i.e. accept a long-term perspective. Only “view” forms that idiom; “take the long outlook/gaze/sight” are not English collocations, and “gaze” and “sight” are literal looking. C.

Gap (2) heads a rule-as-written statement that the next sentences set against practice: “That is the clause as written, and nobody disputes it or finds it odd. It is simply not what the list runs on.” “Strictly” (strictly speaking, by the rule) is exactly that move. “Curiously” is blocked by “nobody... finds it odd”; “Increasingly” asserts a trend the passage never gives; “Privately” contradicts a written clause. B.

Gap (3) is inside a named idiom — “The older hands have a phrase for this among themselves, about waiting for dead men’s ___” — and the only phrase in English is “dead men’s shoes,” waiting for a place that falls vacant on a death. It matches the surrounding sense: “Movement comes when somebody else stops... a winter that settles it,” and “It is not affectionate and it is not quite a joke.” Coats, gloves and hats form no such phrase. A.

Gap (4) sits in a two-pole concession: “the tone of that line is not approving, but it is not ___ either,” so the gap needs the opposite pole of approving. “Censorious” supplies it; “gracious” sits on the approving side and makes the contrast collapse, while “cautious” and “anxious” are not opposites of approval at all. The context — a tenancy quietly passing to a nephew, given “one line” in the minutes — is the committee neither blessing nor condemning. D.

Gap (5) takes a rule as object: “The rules say a second refusal sends a name to the foot of the list. The rule has not been ___.” Rules are invoked; the point is that after “Three times the answer was no” the rule was never applied. “Summoned” takes people, “provoked” takes reactions, and “evoked” takes memories or feelings — the near-homophone trap. C.

The passage says height, not pattern, carries information: “The pot that stands a course above its neighbours belongs to a flue that smoked, usually the shortest one on the stack.” That is A. B is contradicted by the stated reason for a narrow mouth — “since the same gases leave faster through less of an opening” (rain and birds are never mentioned); C by “Pattern tells you very little”; D by “Builders’ yards sold whatever was in stock” and “a stack rebuilt in 1961 carries what came off the lorry.”

The figures are the whole item: the chandler’s hatch “opened at seven in the morning and took in 412 letters; the bookseller’s opened at two and took in 390,” and “Both shut when the evening cart went at eight” — thirteen hours against six for twenty-two more letters. That kills B (412 vs 390 is not “far more”) and C (both shut at eight, so the bookseller stayed open after nothing). A is the strongest near-miss, since the keeper “was allowed threepence for every hour the hatch stood open, and not a penny for the letters themselves,” but it says “the keepers” stretched their hours and the bookseller “opened at two” — a six-hour day — so it is not supported for both. D is what the near-equal counts against unequal hours imply.

The sequence is given in order: “Arbetet gjordes sent på hösten, när vattnet i mossen hade sjunkit undan”, “fick ligga ute vintern över” and “Först därefter rostades den”. A inverts both the season and the order (roasting before the heap); B is contradicted by “Långt ifrån varje mosse bär ett sådant skikt”; D by “Utan spettet gick skiktet inte att finna, för på ytan syns det inte”. C restates the passage.

The first of Tolvsäter’s two results is explicit: “De blåsningar som drevs hårdast, med tätare bälgtag och mer kol i varven, gav inte större luppar utan sprödare: kolet gick in i järnet, och klumpen sprack under släggan” — harder driving, more carbon in the metal, more brittle. B reverses it; C overstates it into total failure, which the text never says; D is not a result of the trials — drying is mentioned only in the description of the furnace itself. A.

The solid-state reduction is named as the root of the rest: “Järnet reducerades i fast form”, “Ur detta följer mycket av det som annars ser ut som fattigdom”, “En blåsning gav några kilo järn” and “Tyngdpunkten i arbetet låg inte vid ugnen utan i smedjan efteråt” — both lupp size and where the work sat. A fails on the dating, “Kolet ur tappgroparna daterar bruket till tiden mellan 300-talet och 1200-talet”; B reverses the two technologies, since it was the hytta that “krävde vattenkraft”; C is contradicted by “uppteckningarna... säger nästan ingenting om själva blåsningen”. D.

Tolvsäter’s second result answers this directly: “den järnrika slaggen visade sig vara ett villkor. En slagg med lägre järnhalt blir trögflytande vid de temperaturer en sådan ugn orkar hålla... Järnet i avfallet är priset för att slaggen alls ska lämna schaktet.” A is Krokvall’s reading of “dålig kontroll”, which the trials speak against; C is contradicted by “i flera fall kring en tredjedel” and by dating resting on charcoal; D is excluded by “varken malmens halt eller ugnarnas mått räcker för att förklara spridningen”. B.

The writer withdraws her vote but not the need: “Nu vill jag ta tillbaka min röst” against “Att åtgärder behövs är ingen stridsfråga”, closing with “Köp bojarna, badstegen och hjärtstartaren över driftsbudgeten” — equipment yes, fee-funding no. B is contradicted by the cut line, the short ladder and the absent defibrillator; C by the retraction; A by the fact that her objection is to the mechanism, not the level (“Avgiften vid bryggan lär förskjuta en del av badandet just dit”). D.

The one figure given is “Kommunens egen uppföljning landade på en betalningsgrad om 31 procent av gästnätterna” — so roughly sixty-nine per cent, about seven nights in ten, went unpaid. C inverts it; B is contradicted by the fact that the follow-up produced a number at all; D is never mentioned — the sign is described as still the model (“en skylt, en kod och tilliten till att gästen skannar”). A.

What the anmälningar showed is stated plainly: “I de fall där skriften gick att jämföra med annat i mappen härrörde yrkesordet i regel från abonnenten själv.” A is the opposite of that; C is contradicted by “Titelraden var tom på den tryckta blanketten: ingen lista över godkända ord”; B goes past the evidence, since the text says the strikeouts “kan lika gärna vara ändrade beslut som rättelser av en felläsning – materialet svarar inte på det”. D.

She concedes: “Ingen av mina tre mekanismer fanns alltså. Jag får ge Rämnestad rätt, och den förklaring som från början låg närmast är också den som står kvar” — and that nearest explanation was the ordinary one, “Den förklaring som ligger närmast är fåfänga.” A is contradicted by “Jag får ge Rämnestad rätt”; D by “Ingen av mina tre mekanismer fanns”, which leaves nothing to combine; C overreads the residue — “Ett par saker får jag ändå inte att gå ihop” concerns loose details, not the main question, which she does settle. B.
